item.title: JavaScript Object Key Definition Using Computed Properties vs Bracket Notation
item.description:
“JavaScript Object Key Definition Using Computed Properties vs Bracket Notation”

When constructing JavaScript objects, the need often arises to use the value of a variable or expression as the property key, rather than a static string. This technique is particularly useful when mapping constants or dynamic identifiers to specific values, such as mapping type constants to corresponding UI icons.

Implementing Dynamic Keys: ES6 Computed Property Names

If your execution environment supports ES6 features (often through modern browsers or transpilers like Babel), the most syntactically elegant approach is leveraging Computed Property Names. This allows you to place an expression within square brackets [] directly within the object literal definition.
